unit.subject: English
unit.unitOverview: In this unit you will learn the words for the people in your family — mum, dad, sister, brother, grandma and grandpa. You will also learn some breakfast and fruit words, and how to count from 1 to 10. You will talk about who is in your family, and about how families help each other and have fun together. Say the words out loud — this is about talking with confidence, not perfect spelling.
unit.learningPath:
Begin with the guided teacher launch and learn a few words through pictures and play.
Listen to the Unit story and join in with repeated language.
Complete six language, speaking, early-writing and practical activities.
If you have access to live teacher sessions, meet your teacher three times each week for two weeks for extra practice — these are optional, and every skill in this unit is also fully covered through the teacher launch, story, and speaking and writing activities above.
Finish the ten-question checkpoint, then tell an adult what you can do if one is nearby — or say it out loud to yourself.

readings.title: Breakfast at Grandma's House
readings.setting: Home, online lesson or Grade 1 classroom
readings.passageScript:
It was Saturday morning. Amal woke up early. “We are going to Grandma's house!” she said.

Amal has a big family. She has a mother and a father. She has a little brother named Idris. Idris is a baby. He is very small.

“Come, Amal,” said her mum. “Hold my hand.” They walked to Grandma's house together.

Grandma opened the door. “Hello, my dear ones!” she said. She gave everyone a big hug.

“I love you, Grandma,” said Amal.

Grandpa was in the kitchen. “Good morning!” he said. “Who is hungry? It is time to eat!”

“Me! Me!” said Amal. She was very hungry.

On the table there was lots of fruit. There was one mango. There was one yellow banana. There were ten green grapes. There were four red strawberries.

“Let us count the grapes,” said Grandpa. Amal counted: “one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!” Ten grapes!

“Well done, Amal!” said Grandpa.

“Can I help?” asked Amal. “Yes, please,” said Grandma. “You can lay the table.” Amal put out the little bowls. One, two, three, four, five bowls.

Everyone sat down. They ate the sweet mango. They ate the soft banana. Baby Idris ate his cereal with milk. Some of it went on his nose! Everyone began to laugh.

“Idris is a funny baby,” said Amal, and she gave him a kiss.

After breakfast, the family sat together. Mum and Dad talked with Grandma and Grandpa. Amal helped to tidy the bowls. Then she played a counting game with Idris.

“I love Saturday,” said Amal. “I love my family best of all.”

Grandma smiled. “And your family loves you, little one,” she said.

readings.setting: Home, online lesson or Grade 1 classroom
readings.passageScript:
The “Families” poem — say it together
Some families are big, / Some families are small. / I love my family best of all.
After you say it, ask a grown-up: “Is our family big or small? Who is in our family?” Say the poem three times — a little louder each time!
The “Ten in the Bed” counting song
There are 10 in the bed / And the little one says, ‘Roll over. Roll over.’ / So they all roll over and 1 falls out… (count down to 1) / There is 1 in the bed / And the little one says, ‘Good night!’
Hold up ten fingers and put one down each time. This is a fun way to practise counting backwards.

grownUpGuide.label: Teacher & Parent Guide
grownUpGuide.intro: In this unit, your child learns the words for family members (mum, dad, sister, brother, grandma, grandpa), some breakfast and fruit words, and how to count from 1 to 10. They talk about who is in their family and how families help and have fun together. The gentle idea is that families love and help each other. The goal is warm, confident talking in English — not perfect spelling.

sections.title: 🧭 About this unit (please read first)
sections.body:
Your child is a beginner, about 5–7 years old, and is just starting to read. So YOU lead this unit — a teacher in class or a parent at home.

Work in short, happy sessions of about 15–20 minutes. Lots of pointing, saying, singing, counting and colouring — very little writing.

This guide tells you what to do. The Child Activity Sheet is what your child draws and colours. The Story is one you read aloud.

sections.title: 💬 Using the AI Tutor with a young child
sections.body:
The grown-up holds the device and reads with the child — do not leave a 5-year-old alone with it.

Ask the tutor to say a family word slowly so your child can copy the sound: “Please say the word ‘grandma’ slowly.”

Ask it to count from 1 to 10 with you, or to sing the “Ten in the Bed” song.

Ask it to play a “Do you like…?” game about fruit with you and your child.

Ask it to give you one more simple activity if your child wants to keep going.

sections.title: 🌟 Tips for teaching absolute beginners
sections.body:
Keep it short and playful. Stop while it is still fun.

Repeat, repeat, repeat — young children learn by hearing words many times.

Use your hands, face and voice. Point, count on fingers, act, and smile.

Use real family photos and real fruit at home — it makes the words come alive.

Praise every try. Confidence matters more than being correct at this stage.

sections.title: What Your Child Will Be Able to Do
items: Name the people in a family (mother, father, sister, brother, grandma, grandpa, baby).
Name some breakfast foods and fruits (pancakes, cereal, milk, mango, banana, grapes).
Count from 1 to 10, and count backwards from 10 to 1.
Ask and answer simple questions: “Do you like bananas?” → “Yes, I do.” / “No, I don't.”
Say what their family does together (help, work, play, eat, talk, laugh).
Hear the short ‘a’ sound in words like cat, hat and map.
Join in the “Families” poem and the “Ten in the Bed” counting song.

items: Family members: mother / mum · father / dad · sister · brother · grandma · grandpa · family · baby · grown-ups · children
Breakfast and food: pancakes · cereal · milk · noodles · fruit · mango · banana · grapes · strawberries · watermelon
Numbers: one · two · three · four · five · six · seven · eight · nine · ten

sections.title: Songs and Rhymes
sections.body:
The “Families” poem — say it together

Some families are big, / Some families are small. / I love my family best of all.

After you say it, ask your child: “Is our family big or small? Who is in our family?” Say the poem three times — a little louder each time!

The “Ten in the Bed” counting song

There are 10 in the bed / And the little one says, ‘Roll over. Roll over.’ / So they all roll over and 1 falls out… (count down to 1) / There is 1 in the bed / And the little one says, ‘Good night!’

Hold up ten fingers and put one down each time. This is a fun way to practise counting backwards.

sections.title: How to Teach This Unit, Step by Step
sections.body:
Repeat this simple shape over several short sessions:

1. Warm-up (2–3 min)

Greet your child: “Hello! How are you today?”

Count together from 1 to 10 on your fingers.

2. Learn the words (5 min)

Point to a family photo (or a picture) and say the word clearly: “mum”. Ask your child to repeat.

Do 4–5 words at a time. Use big smiles and lots of praise.

3. Play and sing (5 min)

“How Many?” game: point around the room and ask “How many chairs are there?” Count them together.

Sing “Ten in the Bed”, putting a finger down for each one that rolls out.

4. Story time (5 min)

Read the Story file, “Breakfast at Grandma's House”, aloud. Point to the pictures your child draws and ask the simple talk-about questions.

5. Activity sheet (5 min)

Sit with your child and do one or two activities from the Child Activity Sheet. Read each instruction aloud for them.

6. Wrap-up (2 min)

Ask: “Who is in your family? What do we do together?” Celebrate! Say “Well done!” and one thing they did well.

sections.title: Sentence Patterns to Say Out Loud
sections.body: Speaking comes before writing. Practise these spoken patterns often:
items: “This is my ______.” (mum, dad, sister, brother)
“I eat ______ for breakfast.”
“Do you like ______?” → “Yes, I do.” / “No, I don't.”
“How many ______ are there?” → “There are ______.”
“I help my family. I can ______.” (tidy, play, lay the table)

sections.title: Simple Check — What to Look For
sections.body: You do not need a test. Just watch and tick when your child can do these:
items: Names 4 family members.
Counts from 1 to 10.
Counts backwards from 10 to 1.
Answers “Do you like…?” with “Yes, I do.” or “No, I don't.”
Says one way they help their family.
